name: Gear / direction / pairing status word

enum.4: Reversing — motor is being commanded to run in reverse
enum.5: Rolling — the wheel/vehicle is currently in motion

explain: Little-endian 16-bit word formed from payload bytes 0-1 (arg[2]/arg[3]) of the id-226 dashboard frame; carries gear, drive mode, motion and pairing flags read every telemetry cycle.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L18 (gear:Int, name only — Worthless models gear as a plain scalar, not this bit-packed word, so it does not corroborate the packing itself)
notes: Bits 0-1 pack the 2-bit gear value (0-3, GraphPage.cs#L1516 `m_gear = arg[2] & 3`); bits 2-3 pack a 2-bit drive/XS-control mode (`(arg[2]>>2)&3`); bit 6 is unused in the decompiled source. In the high byte (arg[3]), bits 11-12 (word-relative) pack a 2-bit PassOk/unlock-progress code (`(arg[3]&0x18)>>3`, GraphPage.cs#L1548) and bit 15 is `function_state` (`(arg[3]&0x80)!=0`, GraphPage.cs#L1552); bits 8-10 and 13-14 are unused/unconfirmed. decode_telemetry() returns the raw 16-bit word for bitfield entries — callers must mask these multi-bit sub-fields themselves; this schema has no bit-mask type to isolate them as separate scalar keys.

name: Fault / stop status word

enum.4: Over-voltage alarm (if status_word_2 bit 15 set) / Under-voltage alarm (otherwise)
enum.10: Phase short-circuit fault (if status_word_1 bit 11 clear) / Phase-lost alarm (if set)
enum.15: Stop state active (App.Stop) — not one of the 15 numbered faults above

explain: Little-endian 16-bit word formed from payload bytes 2-3 (arg[4]/arg[5]) of the id-226 dashboard frame; each low bit is a numbered fault the official app concatenates into its on-screen alarm message.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FaultEntry.java#L20-L21 (errorFlags1/errorFlags2: Int — structurally corroborates two separate fault-flag integer words, not the exact bit-for-bit packing or a single merged word)
notes: Official source keeps this as two separate bytes, arg[4] (bits 0-7 here) and arg[5] (bits 8-14, plus bit 15 = the stop flag, here); this entry merges them into one little-endian u16 purely so decode_telemetry can slice it with the schema's fixed-width numeric types — bit numbering above is relative to the merged word, not the original per-byte numbering in the fault-message text (which restarts at 1 per byte and skips '16.Brake Alarm', a different frame's field: motor_stop_state, id 250/cmd 0xB2). Bits 4 and 10's exact meaning depends on status_word_2 (frame 0xB3 offset 4) bit 15 and status_word_1 (frame 0xB3 offset 2) bit 11 respectively, both cited above.

name: Modulation index
explain: PWM modulation depth, raw byte divided by 128 to give a 0-1(ish) ratio; higher values mean the controller is driving closer to its voltage ceiling.

name: Motor rotation speed
explain: Motor's measured electrical rotation speed, read as a signed 16-bit little-endian word so a reversed direction can show as negative.
notes: ParaPage.cs's own ReadParaMeter handler decodes the identical two bytes as App.rotation via an UNSIGNED cast (`(ushort)(arg[9]*256+arg[8])`, ParaPage.cs#L895); GraphPage.cs's dashboard handler decodes them SIGNED (`(short)(...)`, stored in m_MeasureSpeed). This entry follows the signed (GraphPage) interpretation since that is the page that actually renders live rider telemetry; docs/protocol.md's earlier §4.1 worked example already treats these bytes as unsigned for a purely-positive 1500rpm value, which is consistent either way (positive values decode identically signed or unsigned).

name: Battery/bus voltage
explain: Battery pack voltage as measured by the controller, raw value in tenths of a volt.

name: Battery/bus (line) current
explain: Line current drawn from/returned to the battery, raw value in quarter-amp counts; sign indicates regen vs. drive.

name: Throttle depth, raw ADC counts
explain: Raw throttle-position reading the controller reports back, displayed by the app as an unscaled count alongside the calibrated throttle voltage.

name: Throttle voltage
explain: Calibrated throttle signal voltage, raw value in hundredths of a volt; updates once per full telemetry cycle rather than every frame.
notes: This is logical id 130 in ParaPage.cs's FlashReadAddr table (index 25 of 55, ParaPage.cs#L177-184), so cmd = 0x80|25 = 0x99. Unlike ids 226/232/238 (frames 0x80-0x82), which the controller re-sends every 7th frame, id 130 appears once per full 55-frame cycle — the throttle voltage updates less often than the other electrical readings, matching its role as a calibration/diagnostic reading rather than a fast control-loop input.

name: Global status word 1

enum.8: Seat/bucket-switch confirmed OK (clear = warning icon shown)
enum.11: Phase-lost condition present (changes fault_status_word bit 10's meaning to Phase-lost)

explain: Global_state1 in the decompiled source: a 16-bit status word read from the id-214 frame that several other fault/UI decisions branch on.

name: Global status word 2

enum.3: Field-weakening (weak-field) mode active; clear = MTPA control
enum.15: Over-voltage condition present (changes fault_status_word bit 4's meaning to Over-voltage)

explain: Global_state2 in the decompiled source: a second 16-bit status word from the id-214 frame, covering field-weakening and walk-assist state.

name: Global status word 3

enum.0: Brake indicator active (dashboard shows a brake icon instead of the roll-direction icon)

explain: Global_state3 in the decompiled source: a third 16-bit status word from the id-214 frame, driving the brake and side-stand dashboard icons.

name: Global status word 4 (unconfirmed)
explain: Global_state4 in the decompiled source: assigned from the id-214 frame but no bit within it is ever read anywhere else in the app.
notes: Included for completeness/parity with status_word_1-3, which share the same frame and assignment statement — decode_telemetry returns its raw 16-bit value like any other bitfield, but no bit meaning is documented here because none was found. Do not assume any bit's semantics beyond 'reserved/unknown'.

name: Controller (MCU) temperature
explain: Controller/MCU heatsink temperature, displayed directly in degrees with no additional scaling (m_mostemp, labeled 'MCU T' on the dashboard).
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L16 (ctrlTemp: Float, matching field semantics — official's 'controller'/MCU temperature)

name: Motor temperature
explain: Motor winding/sensor temperature, displayed directly in degrees with no additional scaling (m_motortemp, labeled 'Motor T' on the dashboard).

name: Battery state of charge
explain: Battery state of charge as a single raw byte percentage (0-100), copied by the app straight into App.SOC with no scaling.
